paper.title_en: Resonant dielectric amplification of superconductivity at the FeSe:SrTiOT$_3$ interface
paper.abstract_en: Epitaxial monolayers of FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (STO) and related polar substrates exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of 65-70 K, far above the ~8 K value of bulk FeSe. Although coupling to interfacial Fuchs-Kliewer (FK) phonons is widely believed to contribute to this enhancement, the apparent universality of high=T$_c$ superconductivity across polar interfaces presents a striking puzzle. Here, we identify the lower-energy FK mode near 59 meV, associated with the bulk longitudinal optical resonance of STO, as a conduit through which the substrate dielectric response enhances pairing in FeSe. Within a phenomenological Migdal-Eliashberg framework, incorporating the measured dielectric response of STO selectively amplifies the pairing interaction near this resonance and raises the theoretical upper bound of T$_c$ into the experimentally observed range. A similar enhancement is reproduced for FeSe on BaTiO$_3$, while related polar substrates such as TiO$_2$, LaFeO$_3$, and EuTiO3 possess the same key electrodynamic ingredients. We refer to this effect as resonant anti-shielding (RAS). More broadly, RAS identifies the bulk electrodynamic response of the substrate as a pairing amplifier, opening a route toward designing superconducting heterostructures through control of their dielectric environment.
